t: A medieval Bulgarian state restored by the revolt of Peter and Asen in 1185 and ruled from the fortress of Tsarevets in Tarnovo.
Kaloyan destroyed the Latin crusaders at Adrianople in 1205, and Ivan Asen II dominated the Balkans after Klokotnitsa in 1230.
Its Tarnovo literary school shaped Orthodox Slavic culture before the Ottomans took Tarnovo in 1393 and Vidin in 1396.
dyk: After his capture at Adrianople in 1205, the Latin emperor Baldwin I was held at Tarnovo; a tower of the Tsarevets fortress is still known as Baldwin's Tower.
ev: Peter and Asen lead a revolt against Byzantine rule at Tarnovo
Kaloyan destroys the Latin crusader army at Adrianople and captures Emperor Baldwin I
Ivan Asen II defeats and captures Theodore of Epirus at Klokotnitsa
The Bulgarian patriarchate is restored at Tarnovo
Mongol invasion forces Bulgaria to pay tribute to the Golden Horde
The Serbs defeat and kill Tsar Michael Shishman at Velbazhd
The Ottomans capture Tarnovo after a three-month siege
Vidin falls after the Battle of Nicopolis, ending the medieval Bulgarian state
